security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, placeholder URLs, and environment-variable examples in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection, hidden executable code, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior. One low-severity privacy issue remains: examples send local or sensitive documents to Azure without explicit data-handling guidance.

remediation.issue: Sensitive document handling lacks explicit privacy guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note to obtain user consent, avoid unnecessary PII, and confirm Azure region, retention, and compliance settings before upload.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Document Upload Requires Explicit User Consent
semantic_findings.description: The documentation shows reading a local document and sending base64 content to Azure. Supported models include IDs, health insurance cards, contracts, and bank statements. The service use is expected, but the skill lacks explicit privacy warnings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly show local file contents passed to Document Intelligence and list sensitive document categories. The finding is about missing privacy guidance, not malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable document extraction without memorizing SDK patterns. This skill provides TypeScript examples for Azure Document Intelligence analysis, models, classifiers, and polling.
actual_capabilities: Shows REST SDK installation and imports for TypeScript projects.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential and API key authentication patterns.
Provides examples for URL and local file document analysis.
Maps common prebuilt model IDs to document extraction tasks.
Shows invoice, receipt, classifier, custom model, pagination, and polling patterns.
limitations: It does not run Azure analysis by itself or include a complete application.
It requires an Azure Document Intelligence resource and valid credentials.
It does not cover every SDK option, region setting, or compliance requirement.
Custom models require prepared Azure Blob training data outside this skill.

use_cases.title: Add invoice extraction
use_cases.description: Build a TypeScript workflow that reads invoice fields such as vendor, total, and due date.

use_cases.title: Prototype document OCR
use_cases.description: Test layout analysis for PDFs, images, tables, pages, and selection marks before production design.

use_cases.title: Train custom classifiers
use_cases.description: Create examples for custom models and document classifiers backed by Azure Blob training data.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a document URL
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a hosted PDF or image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show how to analyze a document URL with Azure Document Intelligence in TypeScript. Include authentication, model choice, polling, and result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Extract invoice fields
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for accounts payable data capture.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a TypeScript invoice extraction flow. Show which prebuilt model to use, which fields to read, and how to handle missing values.

prompt_templates.title: Process a local file safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for files stored on the application server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a local file analysis pattern. Include base64 input, privacy checks, credential handling, polling, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan custom models and classifiers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for specialized document sets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a custom model and classifier workflow. Include Azure Blob training sources, model IDs, classifier document types, polling, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Analyze a hosted invoice with the prebuilt invoice model.
output: The response reports the analyzed page count and detected tables.
The invoice summary includes vendor name, total amount, and due date.
The guidance explains how to check confidence before accepting fields.

output_examples.input: Review a receipt extraction workflow for a TypeScript service.
output: The result lists merchant name, total, and line item descriptions.
The workflow waits for the long-running operation before reading fields.
The notes call out error handling for unexpected service responses.

output_examples.input: Create a plan for an invoice versus receipt classifier.
output: The plan separates training data prefixes for each document type.
It explains the classifier build request and polling process.
It identifies Azure Blob SAS URL handling as a credential-sensitive step.

best_practices: Use environment variables or managed identity for credentials, and avoid hardcoded secrets.
Check unexpected responses and field confidence before trusting extracted data.
Confirm consent, retention, region, and compliance requirements before uploading documents.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys, SAS URLs, or customer documents into prompts.
Do not assume every extracted field is correct without confidence checks.
Do not use custom models before testing prebuilt models on representative samples.

faq.question: Does this skill call Azure automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript SDK patterns. Your application calls Azure only when you run the generated code.

faq.question: Which SDK does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure Document Intelligence REST client for TypeScript, including polling and pagination helpers.

faq.question: Can it process local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show reading a local file and sending base64 content to the service.

faq.question: Does it store credentials?
faq.answer: No. It references environment variables and managed identity patterns for user-managed credentials.

faq.question: Can it help with custom models?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows custom model and classifier build patterns that use Azure Blob training data.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
